title: Grade 2 Math — Fri, Jun 13
description: Measurement — Day 5 of 5: Mixed — length, weight and capacity
subject: mathematics

questions.question: We measure length in ___, weight in ___, and capacity in ___.
questions.explanation: Length: cm, m, km. Weight: g, kg. Capacity (liquids): mL, L.

questions.question: What unit would you use to measure how much water is in a pond?
questions.explanation: Water volume is measured in litres (L). Ponds hold a lot of litres.

questions.question: Rohan's bag weighs 2000 g. How many kg is that?
A swimming pool is 25 ___ long.
questions.explanation: A swimming pool is about 25 metres long. We use metres for medium-sized distances.

questions.question: A mango weighs 200 ___.
questions.explanation: A mango is small and light — we measure it in grams (g).

questions.question: Priya drank 250 mL of juice. Her mum drank 1 L. How much more did Mum drink?
A pencil box is 20 cm long. A book is 30 cm long. Together, how long are they?
Which is the odd one out for measuring weight?
questions.explanation: Gram and kilogram measure weight. Litre measures capacity (liquid volume).

questions.question: Mom bought 3 kg of tomatoes and 2 kg of onions. What is the total weight?
Which CANNOT be measured in metres?
questions.explanation: Metres measure length and distance. Weight is measured in kg or g, not metres.

questions.question: A milk carton holds 1 L. A small cup holds 200 mL. How many cups fill the carton?
The distance from one end of a classroom to the other is best measured in ___.
questions.explanation: A classroom is about 8–10 metres across. Metres are the right unit.

questions.question: Which weighs MORE — 1500 g or 1 kg?
questions.explanation: 1 kg = 1000 g. 1500 g > 1000 g, so 1500 g is heavier.

questions.question: Ritu walked 2 km to school. In metres, that is ___.
